info.description:
REST API for the credit-report Android app: email/password auth with OTP verification, JWT sessions, profile management, and credit-report CRUD.

All routes are mounted under `/api`. Protected routes require an `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` header obtained from login or email verification.
info.title: Credit Report Service API

get.description: Resolves an account from a mobile number or email address and reports what an account reset would remove from it — reports, orders (and how many were paid for), statements, coupon redemptions and live sessions. Intended to be shown before the reset is confirmed, because those counts are the warning.
get.summary: Find an account by phone or email, with a reset preview

404.description: No account with that phone number or email address

post.description: Deletes everything the account did after signing up — PAN/KYC, credit reports (and their stored PDFs), orders and payment history, bank statements, prefill lookups, OTP challenges and referral credit — clears the profile name and date of birth, and revokes every session. The login survives: the same phone number or email signs straight back in and lands on PAN verification with the paywall restored, which is the point. Role is untouched, so an admin resetting their own account is still an admin afterwards. This is destructive and it is enabled in production; the body must name the account's own phone or email to confirm.
post.summary: Reset an account back to signup

400.description: accountId must be an integer / confirmation does not match

put.description: Grants or revokes a role. 'agent' lets the account issue coupon codes; 'user' is the default. Note that the role rides in the JWT, so a change only takes effect for the target account on its next token refresh — up to one access-token lifetime later.

400.description: Unknown role / accountId must be an integer

get.description: Returns configured offerings, optionally filtered by productType (FD_CARD|SECURED_LOAN) and active. Requires 'bank-offering:manage'.
get.summary: List bank offerings (admin)

post.description: Adds a partner product that helps a user rebuild credit (e.g. an FD-secured credit card): the FD amount, the FD yield, the score band it targets, the estimated point impact, the apply link, and a revenue note. Surfaced by the score-builder toolkit (S28) when the user's score falls in the band. Requires the 'bank-offering:manage' permission.
post.summary: Create a score-builder bank offering (admin)

get.summary: Fetch a bank offering by id (admin)

put.description: Replaces the mutable fields of an offering. Requires 'bank-offering:manage'.

post.description: Marks the named account's KYC row as REJECTED and records why. The reason is required and is shown to the account holder via GET /api/kyc/status, so it should say what to correct. Rejecting an already-verified account withdraws its access — pan_verified is cleared, so it can no longer request credit analytics. The account can re-submit a PAN, which returns the row to PENDING and clears the reason.
post.summary: Reject an account's KYC submission (admin only)

parameters.description: Account id whose KYC is being rejected
parameters.name: accountId

400.description: accountId must be an integer / reason missing or too long

404.description: No PAN on file for this account

post.description: Marks the named account's KYC row as PAN-verified and clears any previous rejection reason. Required before that account can request credit analytics. Needs the 'kyc:verify' permission.
post.summary: Verify an account's PAN (admin only)

parameters.description: Account id whose PAN is being verified
parameters.name: accountId

404.description: No PAN on file for this account

get.description: Returns accounts that submitted a PAN and are awaiting verification, ordered newest activity first (a re-submitted PAN sorts back to the top). The rows carry the full PAN so a reviewer can check it, which is why the endpoint needs the 'kyc:verify' permission. Paged: `limit` defaults to 50 and is capped at 200, `offset` skips rows; `total` is the size of the whole queue, not of the page.
get.summary: List pending KYC requests (admin only)

get.description: Returns configured providers, optionally filtered by loanType (HOME|PERSONAL|CAR) and active. Requires 'loan-provider:manage'.
get.summary: List loan providers (admin)

parameters.description: Filter by loan type (HOME, PERSONAL, CAR)
parameters.name: loanType

post.description: Adds what a lender is offering for a loan type (HOME, PERSONAL, CAR): interest rate, processing fees, minimum credit score, and optional tenure cap. Used by the switch optimizer. Requires the 'loan-provider:manage' permission.
post.summary: Create a loan provider offering (admin)

get.summary: Fetch a loan provider by id (admin)

put.description: Replaces the mutable fields of a provider. Requires 'loan-provider:manage'.

get.description: Returns the configurable recovery window (how many months the switching cost must be recovered within to recommend a switch) and the default foreclosure fees per loan type. Requires 'loan-provider:manage'.
get.summary: Get loan-switch settings (admin)

put.description: Sets the recovery window (months) and default foreclosure fees per loan type. Requires 'loan-provider:manage'.

get.description: The admin view of the catalog. Unlike GET /products this returns inactive plans too, so a retired one can be found and re-enabled.
get.summary: List every plan, retired ones included

patch.description: Updates the catalog price and/or the active flag for one plan. Omitted fields are left alone. Deactivating removes the plan from GET /products AND makes POST /orders refuse it, so it is a real retirement rather than a hide. Price changes are never retroactive: existing orders keep the amount they were created with.
patch.summary: Change a plan's price or availability

400.description: Nothing to change, or a negative amount

get.description: Who referred whom, over a window of whole UTC days. Returns the period total, a leaderboard of referrers (busiest first, capped at 100) and a page of the individual referred accounts. Omitting both dates gives the last 30 days; naming only one fills the other in. `referrerId` narrows the account list to one referrer without moving the headline total or the leaderboard, so drilling in never hides the rest of the period. Rows carry the referred user's phone and email, which is why this needs the 'referral:view' permission.
get.summary: Referral report for a date range (admin only)

parameters.description: First day, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to 30 days before `to`.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: Last day, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today (UTC).
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: Max referred accounts to return (default 50, max 200)
parameters.name: limit

400.description: Unparseable date, inverted range, or a range over a year

post.description: Mails a one-time code to the address the signed-in account wants to link. Optional, unlike the mobile number: a phone signup is complete without one. Refuses an address already registered to another account, and refuses to change an address this account has already linked. Same cooldown / send limits as every other OTP.
post.summary: Send an OTP to link an email address

409.description: Already registered / already linked / resend cooldown

post.description: Checks the code sent by POST /auth/email/send and attaches the address to the signed-in account as a verified identity. Nothing is written until the code passes. Returns the updated profile, in the same shape as GET /profile. No new session is issued. The linked identity carries no password, so email+password login stays unavailable until one is set through the forgot-password flow.
post.summary: Verify and link an email address

400.description: Validation failed / wrong / expired / locked OTP

post.description: Verifies a Google ID token (issued by the Android/iOS Google Sign-In SDK) and returns a session JWT. On first login, creates a verified account; on subsequent logins, reuses the existing account. If the Google email matches an existing account, the Google identity is linked onto it. Requires the Web OAuth client ID to be configured (AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID); otherwise returns 503.
post.summary: Log in with Google

parameters.description: Human-readable device name shown in the device list
parameters.name: X-Device-Name

409.description: Google identity already linked to another account

post.description: Verifies email + password and opens a session for the calling device. Returns a short-lived access JWT plus a refresh token — in the JSON body for mobile clients, or as an httpOnly `refresh_token` cookie when `X-Device-Platform: web`. Send `X-Device-Id` (a stable per-device UUID) so repeat logins update one entry in the device list instead of creating a new one.
post.summary: Log in with email + password

parameters.description: Human-readable device name shown in the device list
parameters.name: X-Device-Name

401.description: Invalid email or password / email not verified

post.description: Revokes the session the access token was issued for and clears the web refresh cookie. The access token itself stays valid until it expires (minutes), so clients should discard it too.
post.summary: Sign out of the current device

post.description: Sends a one-time code to an Indian mobile number (bare 10 digits or +91-prefixed). Unknown numbers are allowed — verifying the code creates the account. Subject to the same cooldown / send limits as email OTPs. Delivered by SMS through MSG91 when an auth key is configured; without one the code is written to the server log instead.
post.summary: Send a phone sign-in OTP

post.description: Checks the code sent by POST /auth/otp/phone/send and opens a session for the calling device. A first-time number gets an account created on the spot (profile incomplete); an existing number signs into its account. Returns the same session payload as email login. An optional `referralCode` attributes a newly created account to that code's owner; it is ignored when the number already has an account, and an unknown or revoked code is a 400 that leaves the OTP usable.
post.summary: Verify a phone OTP and sign in

parameters.description: Human-readable device name shown in the device list
parameters.name: X-Device-Name

400.description: Validation failed / wrong / expired / locked OTP

post.description: Re-issues the signup OTP for an unverified email, subject to cooldown / send limits.
post.summary: Resend signup verification OTP

404.description: No signup found for this email

post.description: Emails a one-time code to a verified email+password account. Returns the same 200 for an address with no account, so the endpoint cannot be used to discover which emails are registered. Call again to resend, subject to the same cooldown / send limits as signup.
post.summary: Start a password reset

200.description: {\"message\": \"If that email has an account, a reset code is on its way\"}

post.description: Redeems the single-use `resetToken` from POST /auth/password/verify-otp and writes the new password. Every signed-in device is then signed out, so the caller must log in again with the new password. The token is spent whether or not the caller keeps the response.
post.summary: Set a new password with a verified reset token

401.description: Reset token is unknown, expired or already used

post.description: Checks the code emailed by POST /auth/password/forgot and returns a single-use `resetToken`, which POST /auth/password/reset redeems to set the new password. The code is consumed here — a wrong code counts against the same attempt limit as signup verification.
post.summary: Verify a password-reset code

404.description: No account found for this email

post.description: Sends a one-time code to the mobile number the signed-in account wants to register. Mandatory for email signups: PAN verification checks the PAN against the account's mobile number, so an account without one cannot complete KYC. Refuses a number already registered to another account. Same cooldown / send limits as every other OTP.
post.summary: Send an OTP to register a mobile number

409.description: Number already registered / resend cooldown / send limit reached

post.description: Checks the code sent by POST /auth/phone/send and attaches the number to the signed-in account as a verified phone identity. Returns the updated profile, in the same shape as GET /profile. No new session is issued — the access token is unaffected, so the client keeps the one it has.
post.summary: Verify and register a mobile number

400.description: Validation failed / wrong / expired / locked OTP

409.description: Number already registered to another account

post.description: Rotates the refresh token and issues a fresh access token. Mobile clients send the token in the JSON body; web clients send nothing — the httpOnly `refresh_token` cookie is read automatically. The old refresh token is invalidated on every call, so replaying one revokes the whole session as a theft signal. Public endpoint: the refresh token itself is the credential.
post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new token pair

parameters.description: Refresh token (omit for web cookie clients)
parameters.name: request

401.description: Missing, expired, replayed, or unknown refresh token

get.description: Returns the account's active sessions, most recently used first. The entry matching the caller's own access token is flagged with `current: true`.
get.summary: List signed-in devices

delete.description: Revokes all of the account's sessions except the caller's own. Use after a password change or when a device is lost.
Revokes a single session by id. Only the caller's own sessions are reachable — an id belonging to another account returns 404, not 403, so session ids cannot be probed.

post.description: Creates a PENDING account with an unverified password identity and emails a verification OTP. Re-signing up for an unverified email updates the password and re-issues the OTP.
post.summary: Sign up with email + password

post.description: Checks the signup OTP; on success verifies the identity, activates the account, and opens a session for the calling device. Token delivery follows the same rules as POST /auth/login.
post.summary: Verify email with OTP

parameters.description: Human-readable device name shown in the device list
parameters.name: X-Device-Name

get.description: Returns a paginated list of the caller's uploads, newest first. Each item carries the id, filename, status, transaction count, and period — not the full analysis (fetch by id for that).
get.summary: List the authenticated account's bank-statement analyses

post.description: Accepts a single PDF under the multipart field "file", persists it in 'processing' status, and queues asynchronous analysis. Returns the created row immediately with status 202; poll /bank-statements/{id} until status is 'completed' (analysis populated) or 'failed' (errorMessage set).
post.summary: Upload a bank-statement PDF for analysis

parameters.description: Bank statement PDF (text layer required; scanned PDFs are not supported yet)
parameters.name: file

400.description: No file uploaded / not a PDF / empty file

413.description: File exceeds the maximum allowed size

503.description: Analysis queue is full; retry shortly

post.description: Public server-to-server endpoint called by Digitap once the user finishes (or cancels) the statement upload on its UI. Not for client use: there is no bearer auth — trust comes from the x-digitap-callback-type header and, when configured, a ?secret= shared-secret query param (the API defines no HMAC in v1.20). Always returns 200 quickly; the report fetch happens after the response.
post.summary: Digitap transaction-complete webhook

parameters.description: Shared secret, when callback-secret is configured
parameters.name: secret

post.description: Calls Digitap's Generate URL API and returns a redirect URL the client should send the user to. The user uploads their statement PDF on Digitap's UI (it never touches this service). Digitap calls our callback on completion; the client polls GET /bank-statements/{id} until status is 'completed' or 'failed'. Available regardless of statement.provider — the client chooses between this and the local upload (POST /analyze).
post.summary: Start a Digitap bank-statement analysis (redirect flow)

get.description: Returns the most recent 'completed' analysis for the caller, with the full derived metrics. Returns 404 if no analysis has completed yet.
get.summary: Get the latest completed bank-statement analysis

404.description: No completed bank statement analysis found

get.description: Returns the analysis for one of the caller's own uploads. When status is 'processing', analysis is null; when 'completed', analysis carries the derived metrics (summary, salary, emis, subscriptions, categories, topMerchants, monthlyTotals, transactions); when 'failed', errorMessage explains why.
get.summary: Fetch a bank-statement analysis by id

404.description: Statement not found (or belongs to another account)

get.description: Returns one of the caller's own uploads including the extractedText (the PDF text layer exactly as parsed). Useful for debugging "why wasn't my salary detected" — the analysis is computed from this text. Never includes the raw PDF bytes.
get.summary: Fetch the raw extracted text for a bank statement

404.description: Statement not found (or belongs to another account)

get.description: Returns the coupons the caller issued, newest first. Holders of 'coupon:admin' (admins) see every coupon instead.
get.summary: List coupons

post.description: Creates a percentage-discount coupon owned by the calling account. Requires the 'coupon:create' permission, held by agents and admins. Omit productCode to have it apply to every product; omit maxRedemptions for unlimited use. The discount is applied server-side at checkout — clients never send prices.
post.summary: Issue a coupon code

409.description: That coupon code is already taken

get.description: What the payment screen calls when a customer enters a code. Returns the list price, the discount, and the payable total, all computed server-side. Reserves nothing — the coupon is only consumed when the order is created, so a quote can go stale if the last redemption is taken in between. Any authenticated user may call it.
get.summary: Price a product with a coupon applied

get.description: Returns the caller's permanent referral code, creating it on the first call. Anyone new who signs up with this code is attributed to the caller — mainly how agents recruit users. Referral codes carry no discount, never expire, and can be used any number of times; each account has exactly one. Safe to call repeatedly: after the first call it is a plain lookup.
get.summary: Get your referral code

409.description: Could not allocate a code; retry

delete.description: Stops future use of a coupon. Agents may only revoke their own; a code belonging to someone else reads as 404 so the endpoint cannot be used to discover which codes exist. Orders already placed keep their discount — revoking is not retroactive.

get.description: Returns derived analytics from the most recent successful credit report: the bureau score, on-time payment %, card utilization %, 180-day enquiries, the graded report card, per-loan interest-reduction (balance-transfer) opportunities under interestSavings, and a single prioritized 'recommendations' list spanning both levers — raising the score and cutting interest. Also includes a scoreBuilder block (journey classification, realistic target, positives, weak-factor diagnosis, and a rebuild/protect toolkit).
get.summary: Get credit insights from the latest report

get.description: Returns a paginated list of the caller's reports, newest first. Each item carries only the report id (unique identifier) and generation date.
get.summary: List the authenticated account's credit-analytics reports

get.description: Returns the derived analytics (bureau score, on-time payment %, card utilization %, 180-day enquiry count, account summary, loan accounts, report card, interest-reduction opportunities under interestSavings, and a unified 'recommendations' list, plus a scoreBuilder diagnosis+toolkit) for one of the caller's own reports, computed from the stored bureau response.
get.summary: Fetch a credit-analytics report by id

404.description: Report not found (or belongs to another account)

post.description: Sends the caller's own report PDF, encrypted, to the email address on their account. Returns 409 when the account has no email — a phone signup that never linked one — so the client can offer to link an address rather than reporting a dead end.
post.summary: Email a report's PDF to the account's address

404.description: Report not found, or no PDF stored for it

409.description: No email address on the account — link one first

503.description: Report storage or email delivery is not configured

get.description: Returns a short-lived presigned URL for the caller's own report PDF, plus the rule for the password that opens it. The PDF is encrypted with the account holder's PAN and date of birth, so the link alone does not expose the report. A 404 means the report has no PDF yet — the relay that fetches it from the bureau is asynchronous and best-effort.
get.summary: Get a download link for a report's PDF

404.description: Report not found, or no PDF stored for it

get.description: Returns the full report row for one of the caller's own reports, including the persisted raw Digitap response body (response_body) exactly as received upstream. Use /reports/{id} for the derived analytics instead.
get.summary: Fetch the raw Digitap response for a report by id

404.description: Report not found (or belongs to another account)

post.description: Builds the Digitap /credit_analytics/request payload from the authenticated account's profile and KYC record (mobile, name, PAN), plus server-generated values (client_ref_num, otp, timestamp), then persists the request and full upstream response and returns the derived analytics (insights) computed from that response — bureau score, on-time payment %, card utilization %, enquiry count, account summary, report card, interest-reduction opportunities, recommendations, and a score-builder block. Only device_ip is taken from the request body; if omitted it falls back to the detected remote IP. Use /reports/{id}/raw to fetch the unprocessed Digitap response.
post.summary: Request a credit analysis from Digitap

parameters.description: Credit-analytics request (device_ip optional; defaults to the caller's IP)
parameters.name: request

201.description: Response header X-Report-Reused: true means an existing recent report was returned instead of a new bureau pull

400.description: Invalid request body / missing profile or PAN / upstream 400

402.description: No unspent score-check purchase on the account — send the user to the paywall

502.description: Digitap unreachable, or returned an unhandled error

503.description: Digitap rejected our client credentials (server misconfiguration)

get.description: Projects the caller's credit score under a chosen set of actions. Builds a toggle-action set from the report's actual signals (positive levers the file has room to improve on, plus two universal negative actions), and sums the selected deltas onto the current score. By default every positive action is selected; pass `actions` (a comma-separated list of action keys) to override the selection. By default it uses the caller's most recent report; pass reportId to simulate against a specific one (must be your own). Deltas are estimates from your file, not guarantees.
get.summary: Score what-if simulator

parameters.description: Simulate against this report instead of the latest (must be your own)
parameters.name: reportId

parameters.description: Comma-separated action keys to select (default: all positive actions)
parameters.name: actions

404.description: No credit report found / report not found

post.description: Accepts a PAN and the full name printed on it, then verifies both against the mobile number registered on the account, using Digitap's Mobile to Prefill API. A match returns a VERIFIED record. A mismatch returns 422 and counts against a retry cap. If the provider holds no record for the number, the PAN is stored PENDING and 201 is returned — the user is not blocked for a gap in someone else's data. A re-submission overwrites any existing PAN and resets verification.
post.summary: Submit and verify the authenticated account's PAN

parameters.description: PAN and full name as printed on the card
parameters.name: request

409.description: PAN already linked to another account

422.description: PAN or name does not match the mobile number, or retries exhausted

get.description: Returns the account's KYC state without exposing the full PAN (only the last 4 digits). An account that has never submitted a PAN gets 200 with status NOT_SUBMITTED — "no record" is a state, not an error — so a client can render the onboarding step directly from `status`. Possible values: NOT_SUBMITTED, PENDING, VERIFIED, REJECTED.
get.summary: Get the authenticated account's KYC status

get.description: Matches each active home/personal/car loan on a credit report to the cheapest configured provider for the caller's score band, and estimates the monthly and total savings of a balance transfer. By default it uses the caller's most recent report; pass reportId to evaluate a specific one (must be your own). A switch is 'recommended' only when its cost (current loan's foreclosure fee + new provider's processing fee) is recovered within the configured recovery window. Loans the report is too sparse to evaluate are returned with status 'insufficient_data'. Rates are indicative benchmarks, not offers.
get.summary: Loan-switch savings opportunities from a credit report

parameters.description: Evaluate this report instead of the latest (must be your own)
parameters.name: reportId

404.description: No credit report found / report not found

get.description: Returns every order placed by the authenticated account, newest first.
get.summary: List the authenticated account's orders

post.description: Creates an order for the given product against the authenticated account and registers it with Cashfree. The response carries `paymentSessionId` and `mode`, which the frontend passes to the Cashfree JS SDK to open checkout.
post.summary: Create an order and start checkout

400.description: Invalid JSON body / productCode missing or unknown

409.description: Product is not available for purchase

502.description: Payment gateway could not create the order

get.description: Returns a single order owned by the authenticated account. If the order is still awaiting payment its status is reconciled against Cashfree before being returned, so this is the endpoint to poll after checkout closes.
get.summary: Get one order

parameters.description: Order id returned from order creation
parameters.name: orderId

post.description: Server-to-server endpoint called by Cashfree on payment success/failure. Not for client use: there is no bearer auth, trust comes from the `x-webhook-signature` HMAC over the raw body, and `x-idempotency-key` de-duplicates redeliveries.
post.summary: Cashfree payment webhook

parameters.description: Cashfree delivery id, used to drop duplicates
parameters.name: x-idempotency-key

get.description: Reports whether the service is up.
get.summary: Liveness check

get.description: Returns the active product catalog with prices. Use a product's `code` as the `productCode` when creating an order.
get.summary: List purchasable products

get.description: Returns the full account record for the current session, plus a "kyc" block carrying the account's KYC state (status, panVerified, last 4 of the PAN). Clients should read KYC completion from here rather than tracking it locally.
get.summary: Get the authenticated account's profile

put.description: Sets first/last name (required) and optional date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD), marking the profile step complete.

referredByAccountId.description: Referral attribution, set once at signup and never changed.

tokenEpoch.description:
TokenEpoch after the reset. Every access token minted before it is dead,
which is how the target lands back on the login screen.

applyUrl.description: ApplyURL is the CTA destination for taking up the product.

estimatedPointsMin.description:
EstimatedPointsMin/Max bound the estimated score gain. Always rendered with
the "estimated, not guaranteed" disclaimer.

interestRatePercent.description:
InterestRatePercent is the FD yield for display (the deposit keeps earning
while the card builds history). Not a borrowing rate.

minCreditScore.description:
ScoreBand gates the offering: it is surfaced only when the user's score is
within [MinCreditScore, MaxCreditScore]. Defaults 0..900 = "everyone".

minFdAmount.description:
MinFDAmount is the fixed deposit the user opens to obtain the product
(e.g. a card against the FD). 0 when not applicable.

revenueNote.description: RevenueNote is an ops-facing referral/commission note.

analysis.description:
Analysis is the derived metrics (salary, EMI, categories, ...). Nil until
the row reaches status 'completed'. For local rows it's our Analysis
struct; for digitap rows it's Digitap's report JSON, stored verbatim.

errorMessage.description: ErrorMessage is set only when Status == 'failed'.

extractedText.description:
ExtractedText is the PDF text layer. Empty until the worker runs.
Local-provider rows only; digitap rows leave this null.

provider.description:
Provider records which flow produced this row: 'local' (the client
uploaded a PDF we parse in-process) or 'digitap' (the user uploaded to
Digitap's UI and we fetched the report). Drives the poll fallback and how
the client interprets the analysis payload.

requestId.description:
Digitap-flow fields. Populated for provider='digitap' rows; null otherwise.
RequestID/RedirectURL/URLExpiresAt are set at initiation; TxnID is filled
in when the callback or status-check first names the transaction.

createdBy.description: CreatedBy is the issuing account — the agent this redemption attributes to.

productCode.description: ProductCode nil means the coupon applies to every product.

creditScore.description:
CreditScore is the bureau score (SCORE.BureauScore) lifted out of the
response at write time. Nil when the pull failed or returned no record.

resultPdfUrl.description:
ResultPDFURL is the s3:// URI of the stored PDF report, not a URL anyone
can follow: the bucket is private, so reads are presigned at request time.
Digitap returns a link that lives about an hour (result_pdf); we download
it, encrypt it with the holder's PAN + date of birth and upload it
asynchronously. Nil until that completes, if it failed (best-effort), or
if no password could be built — an unprotectable report is not stored.
Mirrors the creditScore lift-out.

agent.description:
Agent is parsed by the server from the User-Agent header. Best-effort:
unrecognized agents leave fields empty rather than guessing.

client.description:
Client is whatever the app declared via X-Device-Info: make, model, OS
version, app version, and any extra keys it cares to send. Free-form but
bounded (see middleware.parseDeviceInfoHeader) because it is user input.

reviewedByAccountId.description:
ReviewedByAccountID / ReviewedAt record which admin made the last
verify-or-reject decision and when. Both are NULL until someone reviews
the submission, and are cleared again if the applicant re-submits.

createdAt.description:
CreatedAt is when the account first submitted a PAN; UpdatedAt is when
the record last changed, and is what the queue is ordered by — a
re-submitted PAN needs review again, so it belongs back at the top.

CreatedAt is when the account first submitted a PAN; UpdatedAt is when
the record last changed (a re-submission or a verification).

panLast4.description:
PANLast4 is the tail of the PAN on file, enough for the user to recognise
which number they submitted. Empty when nothing is on file.

rejectionReason.description:
RejectionReason is set only on a REJECTED record; it is what the client
shows the user so they know what to correct before re-submitting.

status.description: Status is one of KycNotSubmitted / KycPending / KycVerified / KycRejected.

amount.description:
Amount is what the customer is charged, i.e. already net of any coupon.
DiscountAmount and CouponCode are snapshots of how it got there, so the
list price is Amount + DiscountAmount and later edits to the coupon can
never rewrite this order.

description.description:
Description is customer-facing copy: newline-separated feature lines that
clients render as a checklist on the plans screen.

referredByAccountId.description: Referral attribution, set once at signup and never changed.

profileCompleted.description:
ProfileCompleted is the cheapest signal of whether a referral turned
into a real user or stopped at the OTP screen.

referredByCode.description:
ReferredByCode is the code as typed at signup, which for an older
account may be a REF-prefixed one the referrer no longer holds.

referralCode.description:
ReferralCode is the referrer's current live code. Null when the account
has never opened the app's referral screen — codes are minted on first
read, so an account can have referrals attributed to a code that was
later revoked and not yet replaced.

idempotency_key.description:
IdempotencyKey makes the pull safe to repeat. Optional — omitting it keeps
the old behaviour where every call is a new billed request — but the app
always sends one, because this endpoint costs the user money twice over: a
Digitap call we are billed for, and one of their paid orders spent.

The key must identify the ATTEMPT, not the request: a client that mints a
fresh one on every retry has bought nothing, since the whole point is that
a re-entered screen sends the same key the first entry did.

active.description:
Active mirrors isActiveStatus on this tradeline's Account_Status — the same
test that produces ActiveAccountCount, so the per-account flag and the
summary count can never disagree. Clients split "current" from "closed
history" on this; without it every account reads as closed.

amount.description:
Amount is the charged total, already net of any coupon. OriginalAmount
and DiscountAmount let the payment screen show the saving without
recomputing it — and without being trusted to.

category.description: Category is "score" (raise the credit score) or "interest" (cut interest).

estimatedPointsMin.description:
EstimatedPointsMin/Max bound the estimated score gain for "score"
recommendations (nil for "interest" ones). They are estimates, not
promises — actual movement depends on lender reporting cycles.

impact.description:
Impact is a human-readable, deliberately non-promissory hint at the payoff
(e.g. the current factor state, or the estimated rupee saving).

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the bureau pull ran — what a client shows as "checked on".

derogatoryAccounts.description:
DerogatoryAccounts counts written-off / settled / defaulted tradelines —
the serious negatives the "good news" diagnosis checks for.

interestSavings.description:
InterestSavings holds the balance-transfer opportunities computed from the
report's active loans (nil when the loan-switch feature isn't wired in).

onTimePaymentPercent.description:
OnTimePaymentPercent is nil when no month of payment history was reported
on any tradeline — which is different from 0%, and used to be indistinguishable
from it. A thin or brand-new file showed "0% on time", read as "never paid
anything on time", and graded the payment factor F/Critical off no data at all.
The clients already model this as nullable and render "—".

outdated.description:
Outdated is true once the report is older than reportFreshWindow. Clients
must drive "time to refresh" off this flag rather than re-deriving it from
CreatedAt: the window is a product decision, and two implementations of it
would eventually disagree about whether the same report is stale.

recommendations.description:
Recommendations is a single prioritized list of actions the user can take,
spanning both levers: improving the score (from the report card) and
reducing interest (from recommended switches).

scoreBuilder.description:
ScoreBuilder is the credit-score diagnosis + rebuild plan (Journey 05·C):
journey classification, a realistic target, the positives on file, what's
dragging the score, and a toolkit of strategies to raise it.

drivers.description: Drivers are the factors dragging the score down (weakest first).

journey.description:
Journey is "rebuild" (< 650), "blended" (650–749), "protect" (>= 750), or
"unknown" (no score on file).

positives.description: Positives are the reassuring facts found on the file (no defaults, etc.).

strategies.description: Strategies is the rebuild/optimize toolkit, highest-impact first.

timelineMonthsMin.description:
TimelineMonthsMin/Max bound a realistic time-to-target (0 when the plan is
"maintain", i.e. already at target).

current.description:
Current marks the session the requesting device is using right now, so
the UI can label it and warn before revoking it.

deviceInfo.description:
DeviceInfo is the make/model/OS breakdown, split into what the client
declared and what the server parsed from the User-Agent.

delta.description: projected - current (sum of selected action deltas)

status.description:
Status: "recommended" | "not_recommended" | "no_better_offer" |
"insufficient_data". Reason explains the non-recommended cases.

confirm.description:
Confirm must be the phone number or email address registered on the
account being reset. The admin has already been authorised; this is here
so a mistyped account id cannot delete a stranger's paid reports.

from.description: From and To are the inclusive first and last day of the window.

referred.description:
Referred is the page of individual signups, narrowed to one referrer
when the caller asked for that.

referrers.description:
Referrers is the leaderboard for the window, busiest first. Always the
whole window, so the drill-down never hides who else was recruiting.

totalReferred.description:
TotalReferred counts every attributed signup in the window and ignores
ReferrerID — it is the headline number for the period, so drilling into
one referrer must not make it move. The filtered count is Referred.Total.

message.example: Your report is on its way

expiresInSeconds.description: ExpiresInSeconds is how long the URL stays valid.

passwordHint.description:
PasswordHint states how to open the file. Sent with the link because the
PDF is encrypted and a download nobody can open is not a download.

url.description:
URL is presigned and expires. Not stored anywhere client-side: ask again
rather than keeping it, or a stale link becomes a confusing failure.

couponCode.description:
CouponCode is optional. Only the code is accepted — the discount and the
resulting total are computed server-side from the catalog price, so a
tampered request cannot change what is charged.

referralCode.description: ReferralCode is only honoured when this login creates a new account.

ReferralCode is optional and only honoured when this verification
creates the account. An invalid code fails the call rather than being
ignored, so the new user is never told their referrer got credit that
nobody actually received.

reason.example: PAN name does not match the profile name

referralCode.description:
ReferralCode is optional and attributes the new account to whoever owns
it. An invalid code fails the signup rather than being ignored.

fullName.description:
FullName as printed on the PAN card. Verified against the name the
provider holds for the account's mobile number, with a small edit-distance
tolerance — it does not have to match character for character.
